formation.title: The Eight-Pointed Cross Refounded
formation.text:
The papal bull Vox in excelso is lifted. The Pauperes Commilitones Christi Templique Salomonici, dissolved by Clement V at Vienne in 1312 and stripped from Aragon and Portugal a generation later, are refounded as a sovereign brotherhood. The Castelo dos Templarios above the Nabantia hill is ours; Peniscola or Monzon stands in our name; the Treasurer's chest is opened.

Before the chapter sits a question that has waited a hundred years. Are we the Old Order, the secret-chapter Templars whose bills of exchange once spanned Christendom and whose Latin Rule was written by Bernard of Clairvaux? Or are we the New Order of Christ, publicly papal-sanctioned, the Atlantic mandate of Henry of Sagres made our institutional heart?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: The Old Order Restored: Bernard's Rule, the secret chapter, the Beausant raised.

modifiers.name: The Old Order Restored
modifiers.text: The dissolution is annulled. The brother-knights swear the older oaths under sealed doors; the Beausant gonfanon is raised over the Nabantia hill; the Treasurer-General's chest is unsealed in its medieval form. The brotherhood is feared and isolated in equal measure.

options.text: The New Order of Christ: cross-of-Christ on the sail, Atlantic mandate, papal reform.

modifiers.name: The New Order of Christ
modifiers.text: The reform is accepted. The splayed cross-of-Christ replaces the older emblem on every sail; the Atlantic mandate of Henry of Sagres becomes the Order's institutional heart; foreign postulants are admitted; the bills of exchange flow under papal seal through Catholic Europe.

advances.name: Tomar Convent
advances.text: Master Gualdim Pais's twelfth-century fortress-monastery on the Nabantia hill is preserved as the Templar capital. Charola rotunda, ringed walls, and chapter-house unite cathedral, treasury, and royal court.

event.title: The Castelo dos Templarios
event.text: Master Gualdim Pais's twelfth-century plan is finished at last. The ringed convent-fortress on the Nabantia hill is finished: the Charola rotunda, the chapter-house, the Cloister of the Cemetery, the great cistern. From the keep the eight-pointed cross looks down across half of Iberia. The brotherhood has its visible heart.

options.text: Build it as Bernard intended.

modifiers.name: Castelo Templario
modifiers.text: Master Gualdim's design completed. Tomar's ringed convent-fortress stands as the institutional and ceremonial heart of the brotherhood.

advances.name: Beausant Gonfanon
advances.text: The black-above-white war banner of the medieval brotherhood is raised again. Brother-knight commanderies muster their full heavy cavalry under the Beausant.

event.title: The Beausant Raised
event.text: The Beausant gonfanon, black above white, the fair-and-foul war banner of the medieval brotherhood, is raised again over the Iberian companies. The chapter must decide whom to muster under it: the brother-knights of every commandery, drawn from clergy and minor nobility, or the broad lay confraternities (the milites Christi in minor orders) who supply the bulk of the Order's armed crews.

options.text: Brother-knights: the elite commanderies in full strength.

modifiers.name: Brother-Knight Levy
modifiers.text: Commanderies raise their full armed brotherhoods. Heavy cavalry and brother-knights take the field in numbers unseen since the Holy Land.

options.text: Confraternity militia: the lay brothers and minor orders.

modifiers.name: Confraternity Militia
modifiers.text: The lay confraternities are mustered alongside the brothers. The armies grow larger but less elite.

advances.name: Templar Sergeants
advances.text: The second-class brothers, recruited from non-noble pops as lay brothers. Lighter horse, less armor, but disciplined and free of the noble ban. Buildable light cavalry.

advances.name: The Latin Rule of Bernard
advances.text: The Rule of the Order, written by Bernard of Clairvaux at the Council of Troyes in 1129. Brother-knights live monastically: poverty, chastity, obedience under a single Master.

advances.name: Iberian Preceptories
advances.text: Local commanderies scattered across Aragon, Castile, and Portugal: each a fortified estate with treasury, chapel, and stables. The institutional cell of the Templar network.

advances.name: Bills of Exchange
advances.text: The medieval Templar invention reborn. A pilgrim or merchant deposits silver at one preceptory and withdraws bullion at another under the Treasurer-General's seal. The Order is again the Christian world's first international bank.

event.title: The Treasurer's Chest Reopened
event.text: The medieval Templar invention is revived in our chambers. A pilgrim or a Genoese factor deposits silver at the Tomar preceptory and withdraws bullion at Saragossa, Lyon, or Acre, all under the Treasurer-General's seal. The Convent debates the temper of its lending: a sober writ that sustains the Order's name, or an aggressive chest that fills the coffers but exposes the silver to default.

options.text: Sober lending: the Treasurer's writ is gold.

modifiers.name: The Treasurer's Writ
modifiers.text: Bills of exchange under conservative Treasurer-General oversight. Lending is restrained; the Convent's name is good silver across Catholic Europe.

options.text: Aggressive lending: the Silver Chest is opened wide.

modifiers.name: The Silver Chest
modifiers.text: Aggressive Templar lending: princes, bishops, and Italian houses borrow from the Convent's chambers. Returns are higher; the silver is exposed.

advances.name: The Secret Chapter
advances.text: The closed initiations attributed to the medieval Templars, the rite of the cord, the gnostic acclamations, the kiss of obedience, are codified as the Order's hidden discipline. The chapter cultivates a network of agents under cover of mystique.

event.title: The Secret Chapter Codified
event.text: The closed initiations attributed to the medieval brotherhood, the rite of the cord, the kiss of obedience, the gnostic acclamations whispered in Provencal dialect, are codified as the Order's hidden discipline. The chapter-master asks what kind of brotherhood we should be. An open chapter that admits foreign postulants and dresses the rites as Marian devotion? Or an iron Iberian chapter, hereditary and closed?

options.text: Open chapter: foreign postulants admitted, rites dressed as Marian devotion.

modifiers.name: The Open Chapter
modifiers.text: Foreign postulants admitted; the secret rites dressed as Marian devotion. The Convent gains a wide diplomatic net.

options.text: Iron chapter: hereditary, Iberian, closed.

modifiers.name: The Iron Chapter
modifiers.text: The chapter is hereditary, Iberian, and closed. Brothers swear the older oaths in Latin behind sealed doors. Discipline is iron; foreigners are kept at arm's length.

advances.name: The Cartulary
advances.text: The medieval Templar registries, charters, debts, and estate customs from every preceptory between Provence and the Tagus, are modernised into double-entry ledgers and a unified judicial code.

event.title: The Codex Templariorum
event.text: The medieval cartularies of the Order, enormous parchment registries of charters, debts, estates, and judicial customs from every preceptory between Provence and the Tagus, are codified into a single written law of the brotherhood. The Codex Templariorum stands at the chapter-house: the constitutional foundation of a sovereign banking brotherhood.

options.text: Bind the Codex in vellum and chain it to the lectern.

modifiers.name: The Codex Templariorum
modifiers.text: The medieval cartularies codified into a written law of the brotherhood. The Convent's administration tightens; separatist drift abates.

advances.name: Order Galleys
advances.text: The slim oared galleys of the Aragonese and Catalan commanderies, retasked from Holy Land logistics to Iberian-Atlantic patrol. Buildable galley with cross-of-Christ sailmark.

advances.name: Brother-Treasurer Apparatus
advances.text: The office of the Treasurer-General at Tomar coordinates the Order's finances across all preceptories. The clergy estate gains a permanent stake in the Convent's revenue.

advances.name: Sagres Navigation School
advances.text: In alt-history funded directly from Tomar revenues, as Henry of Portugal funded it from the Order of Christ. Pilots, cartographers, and rutter-writers of the Atlantic, all in Templar habit.

event.title: The Sagres Mandate
event.text: The school of navigation at Cape Sagres is funded from the Convent's chambers, as Henry of Portugal funded it from the Order of Christ in our world's history. The brothers ask what the Atlantic mandate should mean. Some read it as a crusade: a flanking move down the Saharan coast around Granada and Marinid Morocco. Others read it as discreet commerce: gold-dust, ivory, and malagueta pepper running through Templar factories without a single proclamation.

options.text: Outflank the Moor: the African coast is a crusading frontier.

modifiers.name: The African Outflanking
modifiers.text: Templar caravels work down the Saharan coast as a crusading flank. Reach and aggression rise; the diplomatic price is bluntness.

options.text: Quiet trade: the factories work in silence.

modifiers.name: The Quiet Trade
modifiers.text: The Atlantic mandate redefined as discreet commerce. Gold-dust, ivory, malagueta pepper move through Templar factories without proclamation.

advances.name: Templar Carrack
advances.text: The Atlantic carrack with the splayed cross-of-Christ painted on its mainsail. The signature ship of the Order's exploration mandate.

event.title: The Cross on the Sail
event.text: The splayed cross-of-Christ, painted on the mainsail of every Templar carrack from Lagos to the Azores, becomes the universal sailmark of the Order's Atlantic fleet. The Lisbon and Lagos shipwrights are brought into the brotherhood as lay brothers; the ports' caulkers and rope-makers swear minor obedience. The Order's ships fly a sign that doubles as marine identification and sacramental claim.

options.text: Paint every sail.

modifiers.name: Cross on the Sail
modifiers.text: Every Templar carrack carries the splayed cross-of-Christ painted on its mainsail. The Order's maritime presence rises sharply; shipwright pops swear minor obedience.

advances.name: Atlantic Factories
advances.text: Madeira, Arguin, and Sao Jorge da Mina: the armed trading-house at the end of every Atlantic voyage. Half banking-house, half stockade, wholly Templar.

event.title: The Factor-General of the Atlantic
event.text: The factories at Madeira, Arguin, and Sao Jorge da Mina, half banking-house, half armed stockade, multiply along the Saharan and Guinean coast. A standing officer, the Factor-General, is appointed at Lagos to coordinate gold-dust assays, malagueta consignments, and the slave-and-ivory accounts. The Order's overseas commerce gains a single coordinating hand.

options.text: Lagos as the seat of the Atlantic factor.

modifiers.name: Factor-General of the Atlantic
modifiers.text: A standing officer at Lagos rules over the Atlantic factories. The Order's overseas commerce gains a coordinated hand.

advances.name: Cross of Christ
advances.text: The splayed Latin cross with thinner limbs replaces the older Templar emblem. Painted on every sail and pennon, it announces the Order's papal-sanctioned Atlantic mission.

advances.name: Lay Brothers' Confraternity
advances.text: The lay confraternities (laici fratres) attached to each commandery. Soldiers, laborers, and burghers swear minor obedience and supply the Order's overseas crews.

advances.name: Templar Bank
advances.text: The medieval Templar financial system reaches maturity. Bills of exchange, letters of credit, safe deposit, and inter-preceptory transfers, all under the Treasurer-General at Tomar.

advances.name: Baphomet Rumours
advances.text: The trial-era heretical accusations endure as black legend across Catholic Europe. The Convent decides to weaponise them: enemies fear what they cannot prove, and the brotherhood's intelligencers travel under cover of mystique.

event.title: The Baphomet Rumours
event.text: Three centuries after Philip the Fair's trial, the accusations have not died. Idol-worship, gnostic kissing rites, the bearded head called Baphomet venerated in chapter, brothers spitting on the cross at initiation: black legend that travels in pamphlets, sermons, and tavern talk from Lisbon to Lyon. The Convent must choose. Crush the rumours through inquisitorial purge? Or weaponise them into intelligence-network mystique?

options.text: Inquisitorial purge: crush the rumours, restore the Order's name.

modifiers.name: Inquisitorial Purge
modifiers.text: The Convent welcomes a Templar inquisition: heretical rumours are crushed publicly. Domestic confidence rises; the chapter's hidden lore is lost.

options.text: Whisper network: cultivate the mystique, let enemies fear what they cannot prove.

modifiers.name: The Whisper Network
modifiers.text: The trial-era rumours are cultivated rather than crushed. The Convent's enemies fear what they cannot prove; intelligencers travel under cover of Baphomet-mystique.

advances.name: Factor-General
advances.text: The standing officer at Lagos governing the Order's Atlantic factories. A central administration for the Templar overseas mercantile system.

advances.name: Templar Galleon
advances.text: The full Atlantic galleon. Iberian hull, Aragonese fittings, brother-knight gunners. The Convent's standing battle-line.

advances.name: Captaincy of Brothers
advances.text: Madeira, Cape Verde, the Azores: each ruled by a knight-captain answering directly to the Tomar Convent. The militarised governorship of Atlantic colonies.

advances.name: Discount Bank
advances.text: The Order's bank evolves into a discount institution buying mercantile bills at face value before maturity. Transaction-based revenue scales with overseas trade.

advances.name: Tomar Cabinet
advances.text: The Convent's governing cabinet at the refounded Tomar fortress. Eight brothers under the Master manage policy, finance, and fleets.

advances.name: Templar Frigate
advances.text: The late sailing warship of the Order, lighter than the galleon, built for Atlantic patrol of the factory routes.

advances.name: Convent Arsenal
advances.text: The Order's shipyards on the Tagus and the Algarve. Galleons, frigates, and supply ships in continuous rotation; cordage and naval stores from Convent-owned pine forests.

advances.name: Industrial Templar Bank
advances.text: The Convent's bank survives into the age of paper money, joint-stock companies, and colonial commerce. Medieval bills of exchange evolve into modern instruments under the same eight-pointed cross.

advances.name: Convent Free Port
advances.text: The Tomar-Lagos-Faro corridor opened to international commerce. British, Dutch, and French ships put in under Convent flag, paying tolls into the Templar Treasury.

advances.name: Constitutional Brotherhood
advances.text: The Codex Templariorum rewritten as a constitution. The Master is constrained; the eight tongues' representatives sit in chapter; the brotherhood becomes a constitutional banking republic.

advances.name: Continental Clearing-House
advances.text: The Templar bank as the settlement institution of European inter-state finance. Bills of exchange from London, Amsterdam, Marseille, and Hamburg clear through Tomar's chamber. The brotherhood's prestige rests on the silver chest of Christendom.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Brotherhood
destiny.text: The Convent's refoundation calls for a long-term project. The brotherhood's institutional discipline holds; now the chapter sets its eye on a destiny: the secret-chapter banking shadow-empire over Catholic Europe, or the public Atlantic imperium of the cross-of-Christ.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Convent Settles its Long-Term Course
event.text: The chapter has met behind the closed doors of the Charola. The brotherhood's institutional discipline holds; the silver is in its chest; the brother-knights are in their commanderies; the cross-of-Christ flies from Tomar to Sines. The chapter-master poses the question that has waited since the Vox in excelso was lifted: what is the long-term project of the Order? The Templar Imperium of the medieval banker-knight, or the Atlantic Empire of the Order of Christ?

options.text: Set the brotherhood on its destiny.

destiny.name: Continental Commanderies
destiny.text: The medieval Templar heartland. Restore the Provencal preceptories around Avignon and the Champagne mother-house at Troyes, where Bernard wrote the Latin Rule in 1129. The continental commandery network is the spine of the shadow-empire.

conditions.text: the Old Order Restored path
Own Avignon, or a subject owns it
Own Troyes, or a subject owns it
Stability at least 25

event.title: The Continental Commanderies Restored
event.text: Avignon's preceptory rides under the eight-pointed cross again; the mother-house at Troyes, where Bernard's Rule was set down in 1129, opens its chapter-doors after a hundred years of silence. The medieval Templar heartland of Provence and Champagne is institutional once more, and the Convent's brother-knights ride the old commandery-roads of Catholic Europe.

options.text: Convene the chapter at Troyes.

destiny.name: Catholic-Court Penetration
destiny.text: The royal treasuries of Paris and Naples take Templar credit, as the Temple of Paris once kept the treasure of France and Templar brothers served Charles of Anjou as treasurers at Naples. The Convent's Treasurer-General becomes the silent intermediary of Catholic state finance. Raise a Templar Preceptory in each city, accumulate 2000 gold, and bind the courts to the chamber.

conditions.text: Own Paris, or a subject owns it
Own Naples, or a subject owns it
A Templar Preceptory stands in our Paris and in our Naples
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Catholic Courts Take the Convent's Credit
event.text: The royal treasuries of Paris and Naples take their loans from Tomar's chambers. The brothers debate the temper of the Convent's reach. Should the Treasurer-General cultivate a quiet, networked influence, hidden in audit-books and discreet advisors? Or should the chapter consolidate hereditary discipline at home, the iron Iberian brotherhood at full strength behind the Templar bank?

options.text: The Treasurer's court network: discreet, advisorial, audit-driven.

modifiers.name: The Treasurer's Court Network
modifiers.text: The Convent's chambers hold the silver of the Catholic courts. Loan capacity grows; advisor cultivation cheapens. Naval matters are neglected in the chamber-house's shadow.

options.text: The Iron Brotherhood: hereditary, levied, disciplined.

modifiers.name: The Iron Brotherhood
modifiers.text: The chapter is hereditary, Iberian, and disciplined. Nobles' commanderies levy at full strength; the clergy estate's tithe runs through the Convent's audit; brother-knights recover quickly between battles.

destiny.name: The Templar Shadow-Empire
destiny.text: Hold London, Rome, and Lyon: the great Catholic courts, the papal seat, and the Rhone-Saone banking artery all pass through Tomar's chamber. With 3000 gold and 75 prestige, the Grand Chapter rises as the Convent's secret heart.

conditions.text: Own London, or a subject owns it
Own Rome, or a subject owns it
Own Lyon, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 3000
Prestige at least 75

event.title: The Templar Shadow-Empire Complete
event.text: London's Treasury, Rome's Camera Apostolica, and Lyon's bourse all settle through Tomar. The brotherhood is the silent magistracy of Catholic state finance. The chapter must decide its public face: a silent dominion, moving by lightning annexations and unseen hands? Or an openly proclaimed Grand Magisterium, the Order acknowledged as Catholic Europe's banking magistracy?

options.text: The Silent Dominion: forced marches, lightning annexations, unseen hand.

modifiers.name: The Silent Dominion
modifiers.text: The shadow-empire moves in silence. Brother-knight columns force-march; minor courts are annexed before they can call for help. Supply lines stretch thin in the rush.

options.text: The Grand Magisterium: open, magisterial, the brotherhood in honor.

modifiers.name: The Grand Magisterium
modifiers.text: The Convent rules openly as Catholic Europe's banking magistracy. Brother-knight tradition is preserved across campaigns; the peasantry under Templar lordship prosper.

destiny.name: The Atlantic Islands Secured
destiny.text: The three island-clusters from which the Atlantic wind-routes are commanded: Funchal in Madeira, Ponta Delgada in the Azores, and Teguise in the Canaries. The Templar habit replaces the older flags above the harbors.

conditions.text: the New Order of Christ path
Own Funchal, or a subject owns it
Own Ponta Delgada, or a subject owns it
Own Teguise, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Atlantic Islands Under the Cross
event.text: Funchal's harbor in Madeira, Ponta Delgada's roadstead in the Azores, Teguise's stone wharf in the Canaries: three island-clusters under the splayed cross-of-Christ. The Atlantic wind-routes, the trade-winds and the westerlies that command every voyage between Europe and the southern coast, are now ours to enter and leave at will.

options.text: The Atlantic is opened to the brotherhood.

destiny.name: The African Atlantic Outposts
destiny.text: Hold Arguin on the Mauritanian coast and Cabo Corso on the Gold Coast. Raise a castle at each, as the Order of Christ fortified Arguin in 1445 and Mina in 1482, and accumulate 2000 gold. The factor-system drives gold-dust, malagueta, and ivory through the Convent's ledgers.

conditions.text: Own Arguin, or a subject owns it
Own Cabo Corso, or a subject owns it
A Castle or a later fort stands in our Arguin and in our Cabo Corso
Gold at least 2000

event.title: Arguin and Cabo Corso
event.text: The factor at Arguin counts the malagueta; the chapel at Cabo Corso (Sao Jorge da Mina) blesses the gold-dust into Tomar's seal. The brothers debate the African mandate. Should the Convent press it as a Mauritanian crusade, the cross-of-Christ at the prow of caravels burning Marinid harbors? Or run a quiet factor's circuit, ledger-driven, under the cover of Templar coin?

options.text: The Mauritanian Crusade: a flank around Granada and the Marinids.

modifiers.name: The Mauritanian Crusade
modifiers.text: The Sagres mandate read as a crusade. Templar caravels burn Marinid harbors along the Saharan coast; the Order's naval prestige rises with every sail.

options.text: The Factor's Circuit: silver and ivory, no proclamation.

modifiers.name: The Factor's Circuit
modifiers.text: Gold-dust, malagueta, and ivory run through the Convent's ledgers. Trade lanes are protected; burgher pops circulate. The military leadership pool atrophies as silver replaces sword.

destiny.name: The Trans-Atlantic Templar Imperium
destiny.text: Hold Sao Tome on the equator and Maxorata in the southern Canaries. Hold 3000 gold and 75 prestige, and trade sugar through the capital market. The Atlantic Captain-General's Hall rises at Lagos.

conditions.text: Own São Tomé, or a subject owns it
Own Maxorata, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 3000
Prestige at least 75
The capital

children.text: Sugar is produced in the market
Sugar is traded in the market

event.title: The Atlantic Imperium of the Cross
event.text: Sao Tome's equatorial church flies the cross-of-Christ above the sugar-mills; Maxorata's stone factor-house is the southernmost watch of the Canaries. Tomar's counting houses turn the islands' sugar into the Order's coin. The chapter raises the Atlantic Captain-General's Hall at Lagos and debates its institutional form: a hardened sugar-armada under brother-captains, or a chartered colonial brotherhood that opens the islands to migration and burgher-trade?

options.text: The Sugar Armada: brother-captains, convoyed fleets, hardened naval order.

modifiers.name: The Sugar Armada
modifiers.text: The Madeiran sugar fleets sail under Templar convoy. Caravels and galleons run home to the Algarve with their holds full; on-station repair masters keep the fleet at sea.

options.text: The Chartered Brotherhood: charters, migrants, bank branches.

modifiers.name: The Atlantic Chartered Brotherhood
modifiers.text: The Convent issues colonial charters under its own seal. Migrants flock to the islands and the Atlantic factories; the Templar bank's town-branches multiply along the trade lanes.

units.name: Templar Brother-Knight
units.text: The full brother-knight: lance, mail, the splayed cross, riding under the Beausant. Levied through the commandery system from clerical pops in minor orders.

units.name: Templar Sergeant
units.text: The second-class brother: lighter horse, leather, sword. Recruited from soldier and burgher pops as lay brothers in minor orders.

units.name: Order Galley
units.text: Slim Aragonese-pattern galley with the cross-of-Christ on the foresail. The Catalan corso pattern repurposed as Templar coastal power.

units.name: Templar Carrack
units.text: The Atlantic carrack with the splayed cross-of-Christ painted on its mainsail. The Order's Atlantic exploration ship.

units.name: Templar Galleon
units.text: The full Atlantic galleon: Iberian hull, Aragonese fittings, brother-knight gunners. The Convent's standing battle-line.

units.name: Templar Frigate
units.text: The late sailing patrol frigate of the Order, lighter than the galleon, built for Atlantic-factory route patrol.

buildings.name: Tomar Convent
buildings.text: The Castelo dos Templarios on the Nabantia hill: ringed convent-fortress, Charola rotunda, chapter-house, Cloister of the Cemetery. The institutional and ceremonial heart of the brotherhood.

buildings.name: Templar Preceptory
buildings.text: The local commandery of the Order: barracks, treasury, chapel, stables, all behind a curtain wall. The institutional cell of the medieval Templar network.

buildings.name: Templar Banking House
buildings.text: Bills of exchange, letters of credit, safe deposit. The medieval Templar financial invention transposed to a sovereign banking institution. Silver and gold bullion underwrite the chamber's continental network of credit.

buildings.name: Sagres Navigation School
buildings.text: Pilots, cartographers, and rutter-writers of the Atlantic. The school of navigation funded directly from the Tomar Convent's chambers.

buildings.name: Atlantic Factory
buildings.text: The armed trading-house at the end of every Atlantic voyage. Half banking-house, half stockade, wholly Templar. Madeira, Arguin, Sao Jorge da Mina pattern.

buildings.name: Templar Chamber of Credit
buildings.text: The mature Templar bank. Continental clearing-house, safe deposit, letters of credit, discount on mercantile bills. Government-category, the financial cabinet of the Convent.

buildings.name: Brother-Captaincy
buildings.text: The militarised colonial governorship: Madeira, Cape Verde, Azores ruled by knight-captains answering directly to the Tomar Convent.

buildings.name: Convent Arsenal
buildings.text: The Order's shipyards on the Tagus and the Algarve. Galleons, frigates, and supply ships in continuous rotation; cordage and naval stores from Convent-owned pine forests.

buildings.name: Grand Chapter
buildings.text: The Convent's secret heart: the closed chapter-house behind the Charola rotunda, where the hereditary brothers and the silent Treasurer-General convene over the European debt-ledgers. The institutional pinnacle of the Templar Shadow-Empire.

buildings.name: Atlantic Captain-General's Hall
buildings.text: The military-mercantile cabinet of the Atlantic empire at Lagos. Brother-knight captains of every Atlantic colony report; charters are stamped, fleets dispatched, audits heard. The institutional pinnacle of the Atlantic Imperium.

list.name: Sacro Capitulo Generale
list.text: The Sacred Convent General Chapter, the constitutional hub of the brotherhood. Under the Latin Rule of Bernard (Council of Troyes 1129) the Master is elected by the Convent and rules by the consent of the Chapter, which sits annually at Tomar to confirm magistral measures, judge breaches of Rule, and admit postulants. Its members are the Provincial Masters of Aragon, Castile, Portugal, and Provence-in-exile, with the conventual officers (the Seneschal, Marshal, Drapier, Almoner, Treasurer). Magistral acts taken without Chapter consent are nullified by the Visitor-General, the Order's standing auditor of commanderies.

list.name: Apparatus Thesaurarii
list.text: The Treasurer-General Apparatus, the Order's signature institution and the first international banking corporation of medieval Christendom. The preceptories of every province hold vaults open to deposit; a pilgrim or factor depositing silver at one preceptory withdraws bullion at another under a sealed bill of exchange. The Apparatus takes fees on transfer, lends on bond to crowned heads (Philip II of France banked his ransom of the Plantagenets through the Paris house; James I of Aragon mortgaged his crown jewels through Barcelona), and holds the mortuaries of deceased brothers. Its officers are chaplain-clerks under monastic discipline.

list.name: Capitulum Occultum
list.text: The Secret Chapter. The trial of 1307-1314 fixed in Catholic memory the rumour of a hidden inner chapter beneath the open conventual one: closed initiations under sealed doors, the rite of the cord, the kiss of obedience, the gnostic acclamations whispered in Provencal dialect. Refounded as the sovereign Order's standing inquiry chamber at Tomar, the Capitulum Occultum audits the brothers' own loyalty, runs intelligencers under cover of preceptory-business, and weaponises the Baphomet-rumour heritage into mystique that travels in pamphlets and tavern-talk from Lisbon to Lyon. Its officers answer only to the Master.

list.name: Capitanias do Mar
list.text: The Maritime Captaincies, built on the alt-history Order of Christ inheritance from Henry of Sagres. The system divides every Atlantic colony into hereditary captaincy-grants under brother-knight donatarios: Madeira (Funchal, Machico), the Azores, Sao Tome, and the African factor-coast at Arguin and Cabo Corso. Each is governed by a knight-captain who answers to the Lagos Factor-General and through him to the Tomar Convent. The captain holds judicial, fiscal, and military authority over the captaincy in exchange for a tenth of revenues to the Treasurer-General. The pattern is half-feudal, half-conventual; it is the Order's actual instrument of Atlantic empire.

conditions.text: Catholicism religion
